title: Eviction Referral and Reinstatement Standard
content:
An Apartment Home Lease file whose delinquency notice has expired uncured may be referred to eviction counsel under the conditions below, and a tenancy whose case has been filed may be reinstated only as this standard allows.

## Referral

**(a) Status.** A file may be referred to eviction counsel only while the lease is in default, as the lease record shows.

**(b) Waiting period.** A file may be referred only when the frozen date is on or after the cure deadline printed on the delinquency notice plus 2 waiting days. The waiting days are counted as calendar days starting the day after the cure deadline, so the referral date is the last waiting day or any later day. The cure deadline is read from the notice itself.

**(c) Further conditions.** Referral further requires that the default was not cured, that no signed payment plan is in good standing, and that the unpaid rent is at least the floor plan's minimum past-due rent for referral multiplied by the monthly rent. Below that amount the lease stays in default without referral until it is cured.

**(d) What referral records.** The referral records the unpaid rent as the amount referred and posts the court cost under the lease fee rule, and counsel's filing moves the lease to eviction filed.

### Referral dates (hypothetical)

| Cure deadline on the notice | Waiting days | Earliest referral date | A referral dated the day before |
|---|---|---|---|
| 17 March | 18 and 19 March | 19 March | 18 March — too early |
| 30 April | 1 and 2 May | 2 May | 1 May — too early |

### Arrears threshold (hypothetical)

With a monthly rent of $1,700.00 and a referral multiple of 1.00, unpaid rent of $1,700.00 meets the threshold; unpaid rent of $1,699.99 does not, and the lease stays in default without referral until it is cured.

## Reinstatement after filing

After filing, the tenancy is reinstated only when **all** of the following hold:

1. the floor plan allows reinstatement after filing;
2. no judgment for possession has been entered;
3. the resident pays the entire balance due — rent, fees, late fees and court costs — in the floor plan's certified funds instruments; and
4. the lease has been referred to eviction counsel exactly once in its life.

A lease referred a second time is not reinstated and proceeds to judgment.

| Floor plan allows reinstatement | Judgment entered | Entire balance paid in certified funds | Referrals on the lease | Reinstated |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | No | Yes | 1 | Yes |
| Yes | No | Yes | 2 | No |
| Yes | Yes | Yes | 1 | No |
| Yes | No | No (partial, or not in certified funds) | 1 | No |

Whether counsel may settle a filed case on other terms is a legal decision outside this charter.
